sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Devona is a Continental Celtic goddess. Her alternate name is Divona. Little is known about her. She may be the same as Sirona. Sirona was the Gaulish goddess of healing. Springs were believed to heal. Thermal and hot springs carried this power. Devona may have been a spring goddess. The second part of her name comes from a Celtic root for stream. The first syllable means goddess. Koch supplements the record. Sirona appears with 29 inscriptions and many statues. Her name was sometimes spelled Ðirona. She appears beside Apollo, also called Grannus. Her shrine at Hochscheid points to healing powers. She resembles the mother-goddesses, the Matronae. Devona shares this healing character. The source base stands on inscriptions and statues. Her cult spread across Gaul. The healing shrines drew the faithful. The goddess remains linked to warm springs.

okr.objective: Describe Devona as a Continental spring goddess linked to Sirona.
